stem: If a child presents with strabismus, such as exotropia or esotropia, why should a thorough ocular examination be performed?

options.text: It is always a normal 'beauty spot' that resolves on its own.
It may be the presenting sign of an underlying intraocular pathology like retinoblastoma.
It is purely a cosmetic issue that does not affect vision.
It indicates the child needs immediate surgery on the eye muscles.

explanation: Strabismus can occur because the eye is not seeing well due to a tumor or other defect, necessitating a full check.
rationale: Recall the story of the little boy whose 'beauty spot' was actually a malignant tumor.

optionExplanations.A: The text warns against this misconception, as ignoring strabismus can miss serious underlying pathology.
optionExplanations.B: Strabismus can occur because the eye is not seeing well due to a tumor or other defect, necessitating a full check.
optionExplanations.C: Strabismus is often a functional sign of poor vision or neurological issues, not just an aesthetic concern.
optionExplanations.D: The first step is to diagnose why the eyes are misaligned, rather than jumping straight to muscle surgery.
